title: The PreToolUse(Bash) tracked-write gate: #106's mechanical enforcement of the Phase 4 commit-hygiene rule, and its shared run-ownership seam
content:
Landed at #106, merged to main as fc9a171 (PR #113; source commits carry six labelled steps, re-derive with `git log --oneline fc9a171~6..fc9a171` or `git show fc9a171 --stat`). Before this issue, every one of the ten replicated agent contracts' 'Commit hygiene' paragraphs said plainly that nothing mechanically enforced the no-blanket-staging rule for Phase 4 panelists (`git commit -a` / `git add -A` / `git add .`). That sentence is now FALSE and has been retired from all ten carrying files (see the digest entry `architecture--agent-contract-replication-digest.json` for the exact byte-level edit and the new span digests it produced). This entry records the mechanism the sentence now points to.

WHAT IT IS: a `PreToolUse` hook matched on `Bash`, declared in `plugins/pipeline/hooks/hooks.json`, wired to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/pre-tool-use.sh` with a declared 30-SECOND timeout (30000ms, raised from the original figure by commit 54cf51e for #132), still under the platform's 600s default. A command large enough still outruns that declared timeout: at 461,801 command bytes (this repository's own tracked `knowledge/issue-archive/106.json`, staged via `git add -A`) the gate measured deny in 7,366-10,407 ms against the OLD 5000 ms bound (147%-208% over budget, per #132 measured_state), and the worst measured tracked cross-product cell (464,396 bytes, 8.4 bytes per structural character) decided in 24,210 ms raw, projecting past the new 30 s bound too once the spec's load/host margin (1.874x, giving roughly 45.4 s) is applied; when a command outruns the declared timeout the hook is killed, emits nothing on stdout, and the call is ALLOWED (fail open). There is also an explicit fail-open tail for a crashing or missing gate itself: `... || { echo "agent-pipeline PreToolUse: gate unavailable (rc $?); allowing" >&2; exit 0; }`. A crashing or missing gate always allows the call and always leaves one attribution line on stderr.

TWO STAGES, measured and documented in the script's own header (`plugins/pipeline/hooks/pre-tool-use.sh:1-34`). Stage one runs on EVERY Bash call using POSIX shell builtins only -- no shebang line (deliberate: costs one exec avoided per call, measured 6ms vs 9-13ms with one, on darwin 25.5.0), no node, no forks -- and decides the forbidden class over FLAG SEMANTICS rather than spellings: it is quote-aware and evaluates every git invocation in a compound command, so `git commit -aqm m` is refused (bundled `-a`) and a forbidden spelling quoted inside a `-m` operand is not treated as a real invocation. Only the narrow plausible-deny branch starts a node process (`hooks/pre-tool-use-resolve.mjs`) to resolve whose run the call belongs to and whether that run sits at a Phase 4 phase; node cold start measured 66.68ms against a 4.45ms shell baseline on the same host, which is the cost stage one exists to avoid paying on every call. Stage two never receives the caller's actual command string (the forbidden class was already decided in stage one, and a child process's argv is readable by other local users on the host).

THE TRIGGER TERM IS `agent_id`, NOT `agent_type` or a role allowlist. Claude Code sets `agent_id` only inside a subagent dispatch and omits it for the orchestrator's own main thread (even in `--agent` sessions), so the gate refuses ANY subagent-originated blanket-staging call while a Phase 4 run owns the record store -- deliberately wider than the six-role panel (a general-purpose Task worker or an adopting project's own agent is refused too), and the orchestrator's own checkpoint commits are exempt BY DESIGN, not by oversight.

RUN OWNERSHIP, THE SHARED SEAM #106 ADDED. Three new/extended exports in `plugins/pipeline/scripts/validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs`: `bareRole(agentType)` (:383, takes the segment after the LAST `:` so an installed-plugin namespaced dispatch like `pipeline:secops` and a local bare-file dispatch `secops` resolve identically -- also consumed by `hooks/pre-tool-use-resolve.mjs`), `pipelineDirs` (:243) and `activeIssueName` (:312) as shared directory-listing primitives, and `resolveRunOwner(pipelineDirsIn, input, now, ceilingMs)` (:426) which narrows to a CANDIDATE set (no `final_verdict`, and either datable-and-recent or not datable at all) then resolves an owner: zero candidates abstains, an explicit marker naming an in-flight candidate resolves it, ambiguity with no honoured marker abstains. `activeIssueDir` (the pre-existing SubagentStop-sweep answer) is untouched by this change -- it answers a different question ("which dir did this stop just write") and stays in-flight-blind on purpose.

THE PREDICATE MOVED TO A NEW LEAF MODULE, `plugins/pipeline/scripts/run-candidates.mjs`, which exports `IN_FLIGHT_MS` (a second declaration of the 24h ceiling, pinned equal by `tests/test-pretooluse-inflight-ceiling.sh` to the authoritative one still declared in `gate-phase-entry.mjs:189` -- that file's own constant and its exported status is UNCHANGED by #106, see `architecture--gate-phase-entry-inflight-boundary.json`) and `inFlightObservations(status, now, ceilingMs)`, which returns `{concluded, datable, recent, inFlight}` as separate observations rather than one boolean because `gate-phase-entry.mjs`'s phase-entry guard and this PreToolUse gate deliberately read an UNDATABLE record oppositely: the guard EXCLUDES it (abstains, refuses no turns), the gate COUNTS it as a candidate (so it can never shrink a candidate set to one) while never letting it be the resolved owner. `gate-phase-entry.mjs`'s own `inFlight()` function (still NOT exported, still named `inFlight`, gate-phase-entry.mjs:549) now delegates its body to this shared `inFlightObservations` instead of holding its own inline logic -- the module now has a SECOND consumer of the predicate it didn't have at #63, which #63's own recorded claim ('no shared symbol exists anywhere in the tree' -- true only in comparison to pipeline-status.mjs, which #106 left untouched and which still holds its own independent 24h/mtime-substituted literal) does not contradict but is now narrower than it reads standalone. THE MODULE IS DELIBERATELY A LEAF importing from neither `gate-phase-entry.mjs` nor `validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs`, because those two already have an edge (`gate-phase-entry` imports `activeIssueDir` from the validator) and a reverse edge would have turned a fail-open tooling gap into a phase REFUSAL; a caught-in-CI (not in any single worktree) cycle bug during #106's own implementation (`run-candidates -> gate-phase-entry -> validate-pipeline-artifact -> run-candidates`, introduced by a doc-comment that QUOTED the forbidden reverse import) confirms the cycle detector (AC36(a)) reads import edges out of raw source text, comments included.

SIX NAMED RESIDUAL GAPS, disclosed in the ten agent contracts' own retired-sentence replacement (do not restate the mechanism claims from memory; the contract text is the source of record and is reproduced closely there, not duplicated in full here): (1) abstains with 2+ in-flight candidates and no honoured marker -- #111 tracks closing this by propagating an explicit active-issue signal; (2) abstains with zero in-flight candidates, and by construction NO marker can lift this branch; (3) over-refuses non-panelist subagents on purpose (narrowing would reintroduce the role allowlist `agent_id` replaced); (4) suppressible in one tool call from inside the session -- a plain Write of a valid-JSON `status.json` with no parseable `updated_at` enlarges the candidate set and abstains the gate, disclosed rather than closed because closing it would refuse the routine shard writes the gate deliberately permits; (5) a delta round whose record still carries the PRIOR round's `final_verdict` is excluded from the candidate set, so the gate falls silent on a genuinely live Phase 4 run -- that is #110, unfixed by this hook; (6) a `3-impl` fix round (the loop-back destination of a REQUEST_CHANGES verdict) sits outside the guarded phases entirely and is refused nothing.

DISARM: `CLAUDE_HOOK_PRETOOLUSE_SKIP`, read from the hook's OWN environment only (not from any file), operator-set, so no artifact a denied agent can write in one tool call reaches it -- see `plugins/pipeline/README.md` for the knob and for why this gate sits outside the halting-control carve-out that refuses an opt-out for `hooks/stop.sh`'s phase guard.

TEST COVERAGE: five new suites plus five shared fixtures under `plugins/pipeline/tests/` (`test-pretooluse-doc-retirement.sh`, `test-pretooluse-gate-channel.sh`, `test-pretooluse-gate-declaration.sh`, `test-pretooluse-gate-ownership.sh`, `test-pretooluse-gate-verdicts.sh`) plus a sixth (`test-pretooluse-inflight-ceiling.sh`) pinning the two `IN_FLIGHT_MS` declarations equal, discovered by `run.sh`'s existing glob with no edit to `run.sh` needed. `test-pretooluse-doc-retirement.sh` is the one that mechanically checks the RETIRED SENTENCE'S replacement: it byte-diffs the 'Commit hygiene' paragraph specifically (not the full ten/nine-file span) across the nine agent files plus `pipeline.md`'s compressed restatement, failing on disagreement or on a vacuous empty match -- this NARROWS but does not close the pre-existing #19-era gap that no suite checks the full nine-file 'Phase 4 tracked-write isolation' span for byte-identity; see `architecture--agent-contract-replication-digest.json`'s corresponding update for the current span digest.
